instructions: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

items.prompt: Questions 1-3 refer to Passage A01. Work in laboratories had already established that elephants make use of branches in order to (1) ........
items.evidence: Laboratory studies have shown that elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror, remember locations for years and use branches to swat flies.
items.explanation: Paragraf A, laboratuvar çalışmalarının fillerin dalları sinek kovmak için kullandığını gösterdiğini söylüyor; boşluk dalların hangi amaçla kullanıldığını sorduğu için cevap 'swat flies'.
items.flag_reason: Cevap 'swat flies', fillerin dallari sinek kovmak icin kullandigi bilgisinin hayvan davranisi konusunda yaygin bilinen bir gercek olmasi sayesinde parcaya bakmadan da tahmin edilebiliyor.

items.prompt: Pushing a heavy object into place suits an elephant because the end of its trunk stays open and in unbroken (2) ........ with that object.
items.evidence: A cube used as a platform, by contrast, plays to the trunk's strengths rather than against them: rolling and positioning a heavy object keeps the trunk tip open and in constant sensory contact with the object, while also physically lifting the animal's whole body closer to the food.
items.explanation: Paragraf G, ağır bir nesneyi yuvarlayıp yerleştirmenin hortum ucunu açık tuttuğunu ve nesneyle sürekli duyusal temas hâlinde bıraktığını söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'sensory contact'.

items.prompt: A species can look unable to perform a mental task merely because the apparatus it is given does not match its (3) ........
items.evidence: More broadly, the study is a caution against judging an animal's intelligence from a single, narrowly designed test: a species may appear incapable of a mental feat simply because the equipment offered does not suit its particular anatomy, and a fairer test can reveal abilities that had been present all along.
items.explanation: Paragraf H, bir türün zihinsel bir beceriden yoksun görünmesinin nedeninin çoğu zaman sunulan donanımın o türün anatomisine uymaması olduğunu söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'anatomy'.

items.prompt: Questions 4-6 refer to Passage A02. Each pair had a tank to itself, fed with (4) ........ that was held at an unchanging temperature.
items.evidence: Every pair was housed in its own tank, measuring sixty-five by one hundred by fifty centimetres and supplied with running seawater kept at a constant 24°C, so that any behavioural change could be attributed to the animals' experience of one another rather than to differences in their surroundings.
items.explanation: Paragraf B, her çiftin kendi tankında tutulduğunu ve tanklara sabit 24°C'de akan deniz suyu verildiğini söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'running seawater'.

items.prompt: An octopus put back with a partner it already knew delayed (5) ........ and was inclined to hold back at a wary distance.
items.evidence: Octopuses reunited with a familiar partner took noticeably longer to make first contact and were more likely to keep a cautious distance without touching.
items.explanation: Paragraf F, tanıdık bir eşle yeniden bir araya getirilen ahtapotların ilk temasa geçmek için belirgin biçimde daha uzun süre beklediğini söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'first contact'.

items.prompt: An octopus does not have to pick out a (6) ........ ; sorting the animals it meets into two broad groups is enough.
items.evidence: The authors describe this as class-level, or binary, recognition: an octopus need not identify a unique individual by name, so to speak, only sort others into the broad categories of "known" and "unknown" and adjust its behaviour accordingly.
items.explanation: Paragraf G, ahtapotun benzersiz bir bireyi tanımasına gerek olmadığını, karşılaştıklarını 'bilinen' ve 'bilinmeyen' diye iki geniş kategoriye ayırmasının yettiğini söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'unique individual'.

items.prompt: Questions 7-9 refer to Passage A03. What Maug gives researchers is something that no (7) ........ is able to reproduce completely.
items.evidence: Few people ever visit it, yet the shallow waters around it have become one of the most closely studied coral reef sites in the world, because Maug offers scientists something no laboratory tank can fully replicate: a real reef living permanently in the acidified seawater that much of the ocean is expected to experience within decades.
items.explanation: Paragraf A, Maug'un bilim insanlarına hiçbir laboratuvar tankının tam olarak taklit edemeyeceği bir şey sunduğunu söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'laboratory tank'.

items.prompt: Because its reef has already spent years in water the rest of the ocean will not reach for decades, Maug amounts to a (8) ........ of what is coming.
items.evidence: At Maug, by contrast, the reef has already been living for years in conditions similar to those the wider ocean is not expected to reach for decades, effectively offering a preview of the future.
items.explanation: Paragraf C, Maug'daki resifin yıllardır geniş okyanusun onlarca yıl sonra ulaşacağı koşullarda yaşadığını ve bunun geleceğin bir ön gösterimini sunduğunu söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'preview'.
items.flag_reason: Bosluk 'a ___ of what is coming' kalibinin ucunda; bu kalibin en dogal tamamlamasi 'preview' oldugu icin parcaya bakilmadan da tahmin edilebiliyor.

items.prompt: The site is so useful because an actual reef community can be measured instead of a (9) ........ being modelled.
items.evidence: That is the same order of change scientists project for the global ocean as a whole due to human carbon dioxide emissions, which is what makes the site so valuable: rather than modelling a hypothetical future, researchers can measure how a real reef community actually behaves under it.
items.explanation: Paragraf E, araştırmacıların varsayımsal bir geleceği modellemek yerine gerçek bir resif topluluğunun davranışını ölçebildiğini söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'hypothetical future'.

items.prompt: Questions 10-12 refer to Passage A04. In order of distance outwards from the Sun, Uranus comes (10) ........
items.evidence: Uranus, the seventh planet from the Sun, is already known for an unusually crowded family of moons and a tilted, tangled system of rings.
items.explanation: Paragraf A, Uranüs'ün Güneş'ten itibaren yedinci gezegen olduğunu söylüyor; sıradaki yeri sorulduğu için cevap 'seventh'.
items.flag_reason: Cevap 'seventh', Uranus'un Gunes'ten yedinci gezegen oldugu temel astronomi bilgisiyle parcaya bakmadan da bilinir.

items.prompt: Being too small for the instruments of the day to resolve, the moon circled Uranus unseen for almost (11) ........ after the 1986 flyby.
items.evidence: Its size simply placed it below the threshold that Voyager's instruments, or any Earth-based telescope in the decades since, could resolve, meaning the moon had been circling Uranus unnoticed for the nearly forty years between that flyby and Webb's observations.
items.explanation: Paragraf F, uydunun boyutunun dönemin aletlerinin ayırt edebileceği eşiğin altında kaldığını ve 1986'daki geçişten sonra neredeyse kırk yıl fark edilmeden Uranüs'ün çevresinde döndüğünü söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'forty years'.
items.flag_reason: Cevap 'forty years', Voyager 2'nin Uranus'e 1986'da ugradigi ve buradan gunumuze (2020'lerin ortasi) yaklasik kirk yil gectigi genel kronoloji bilgisiyle parcaya bakmadan da hesaplanabiliyor.

items.prompt: At this stage the find counts as (12) ........ , since it has not yet been through peer review.
items.evidence: For now, the discovery remains part of ongoing research rather than a finished, peer-reviewed result, but it illustrates a broader pattern in planetary astronomy: each generation of instruments reveals objects that the previous generation's technology, however capable at the time, simply could not see.
items.explanation: Paragraf H, keşfin şimdilik hakem değerlendirmesinden geçmiş bitmiş bir sonuç değil, süren araştırmanın bir parçası olduğunu söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'ongoing research'.

items.prompt: Questions 13-15 refer to Passage A05. The settlement first came to attention in (13) ........ , although thorough digging did not begin until 1961.
items.evidence: Occupied from roughly 7400 to 6000 BC, it was first noticed in 1952 and then excavated in detail between 1961 and 1965 by the British archaeologist James Mellaart.
items.explanation: Paragraf A, yerleşimin ilk kez 1952'de fark edildiğini, ayrıntılı kazının ise 1961–1965 arasında yapıldığını söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap '1952'.

items.prompt: For the team, the sequences point to an early (14) ........ in the growing of hexaploid wheat.
items.evidence: The researchers interpret this as evidence of an early, transitional stage in the cultivation of hexaploid wheat, and note that this is the first genetic evidence hinting at the presence of a spelt-like wheat in the Neolithic Near East at all, a possibility they treat cautiously given how limited the surviving evidence is.
items.explanation: Paragraf F, araştırmacıların bulguyu hekzaploid buğday yetiştiriciliğinin erken bir geçiş aşaması olarak yorumladığını söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'transitional stage'.

items.prompt: Studying ancient DNA brings to light parts of farming history that the (15) ........ could never detect.
items.evidence: More broadly, the study demonstrates that examining ancient DNA can uncover agricultural history that is simply invisible to the naked eye, since grains that look like one species under a microscope can turn out, genetically, to be something else entirely.
items.explanation: Paragraf H, eski DNA incelemesinin çıplak gözle görülemeyen tarım tarihini ortaya çıkarabildiğini söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'naked eye'.
